blue-catfish: Angler Amy Robison and family went on a recent blue catfish charter trip through the Reelin’ in the Blue Bonanza program, and caught this one near Fort Washington on the Potomac River.
Fishing for blue catfish is very good in the upper Bay tidal rivers this week.
There are always plenty of blue catfish.
bluefish: Anglers fishing along the shorelines of the lower Bay and the tidal rivers are enjoying fun fishing for a mix of striped bass, speckled trout, slot-size red drum, and small bluefish this week.
Medium to large bluefish are being caught in the channels of the Bay by trolling a mix of surge tube lures and umbrella rigs using spoons as attractors and trailers.
Inline weights are needed to get the umbrella rigs down to where the bluefish are.
channel-catfish: The cooler water has a mix of blue and channel catfish moving more freely in slightly shallower waters adjacent to the deeper river and bay channels.
largemouth-bass: Curtis Nelson caught and released this largemouth bass at Deep Creek Lake recently.
Largemouth and smallmouth bass will be waiting in transition areas to intercept them on their move.
smallmouth-bass: Largemouth and smallmouth bass will be waiting in transition areas to intercept them on their move.
Water clarity is good and cooler water temperatures should make for good fishing for smallmouth bass.
Deteriorating grass beds and fallen leaves are soon to come, so enjoy some of the best conditions for smallmouth bass fishing.
striped-bass: Upper Chesapeake Bay Frankie Goff is all smiles with this nice striped bass she caught in the Conowingo Dam Pool while fishing with her dad.
Photo by Don Goff Anglers fishing for striped bass are finding increased success along the shallower shorelines of upper Bay and the lower sections of the region’s tidal rivers.
The Conowingo Dam pool and adjacent Susquehanna River waters are providing good fishing for striped bass this week.
white-perch: Live lining small white perch will work well also.
White perch are holding near structure in the deeper waters of the tidal rivers.
Drifting live spot, small white perch, cut bait, and live eels to the pier bases offers a chance at a slot size striped bass.
